Com «in», o alemão distingue ONDE você e: With «in», German separates WHERE you are (Wo?) from WHERE you're going (Wohin?) — the way English separates "in" from "into", or old English "where" from "whither". Wo? uses the DATIVE: masculine and neuter «im» (in dem), feminine «in der». Wohin? uses the ACCUSATIVE: masculine «in den», feminine «in die», neuter «ins» (in das). To go to a place there's also «zu» (always dative): zum (zu dem) Bahnhof, zur (zu der) Post; and «nach» for cities and countries: nach Berlin. The full cases come in lessons 11 to 13; for now, memorize the chart.
em português a preposição muda («no parq: English changes the preposition: "I'm in the park" vs "I'm going into / to the park". German keeps the same preposition («in») and changes the article instead: «im Park» (in) vs «in den Park» (into). And "to" has three German versions: «in» for buildings you enter, «zu» for people and places you go up to, «nach» for cities and countries.

Pedir e dar direções (imperativo formal): Asking for and giving directions (formal imperative)
Para pedir: «Entschuldigung, wo ist die: To ask: «Entschuldigung, wo ist die Post?» (Excuse me, where's the post office?) or «Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?» (How do I get to the station?). To answer, use the formal imperative: the verb comes FIRST, followed by «Sie»: «Gehen Sie geradeaus.» (Go straight ahead.) «Biegen Sie links ab.» (Turn left — «abbiegen» is separable, so the prefix goes to the end.) «Nehmen Sie die zweite Straße rechts.» (Take the second street on the right.) English drops the "you" in commands; German formal commands keep «Sie». Other useful phrases: an der Ampel (at the light), an der Kreuzung (at the intersection), neben (next to), gegenüber (across from), in der Nähe (nearby).
Take the second street on the left.
Diga: «Entschuldigung, wo ist die Post?: Say: «Entschuldigung, wo ist die Post? — Gehen Sie geradeaus. Biegen Sie links ab.»

Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof? / Como chego: Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof? / How do I get to the station?
A tourist asks for directions on the street.
— A estação? Siga em frente até o semáfo: — The station? Go straight ahead to the traffic light.
— Depois vire à esquerda. A estação fica: — Then turn left. The station is next to the post office.
— Não, não é longe. A pé são dez minutos: — No, it's not far. It's ten minutes on foot.
— Há uma farmácia por aqui?: — Is there a pharmacy around here?
— Sim, a farmácia fica em frente ao banc: — Yes, the pharmacy is across from the bank.
